title: Normalized shifted Tate splitting in the ordinary tower category
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and the strict ordinary derived tower coordinates, operations and given purity data of [def-sp-tower-gamma-data]. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be smooth separated morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e$ over the algebraic closure of a finite field of characteristic different from $\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. All three schemes are separated and of finite type. Fix open/proper factorizations of $f,g,h=gf$, their given adjunction pairs [def-sp-adjoint-compositor-data], and their given diagonal purity records. For the three possibly different presentations of the Tate lines, there exists an actual ordinary derived tower isomorphism $s:L_h\simeq f^*L_g\otimes^L L_f$ such that TowerSplitNormalized [def-sp-composition-orientation-arrow-data] holds: at each positive level its comparison through the prescribed root, coefficient, pullback and tensor words [def-sp-p1-level-words] is precisely finiteLineSplit. This asserts only the splitting, not equality of composite orientations, concentration, or evaluation of mu.

proof.text: Construct pullback of each root line in the strict-system category by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], using the canonical Tate pullback and tensor comparisons of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. These commute with coefficient quotient transitions.

Use the positive tensor-power construction [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Local rank-one freeness [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] makes tensor with each line exact, so the derived tensor of these coefficient lines is the ordinary tensor. Concatenate the e pulled-back factors with the d source factors by the associator, using the root comparisons to identify the three presentations. At zero powers use coefficient-unit pullback and unitors.

Use the simultaneous ordinary tensor and shift models of [lem-pur-diagram-pullback-monoidal-shift-models] to include the shifts. Both shifts are even, hence the sign is (-1)^(4de)=1. Evaluate the resulting actual isomorphism through the specified normalized word comparisons. Their coherence gives exactly finiteLineSplit, including the zero powers and empty scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem tower_tate_split_normalized
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (_hl : l ≠ D.p)
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Z.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (Z ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Z ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Z ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [(jf ≫ pf).IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [(jg ≫ pg).IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (jf ≫ pf)] [IsSeparated (jg ≫ pg)]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d (jf ≫ pf)] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension e (jg ≫ pg)]
    (hcomp : (jf ≫ pf) ≫ (jg ≫ pg) = jh ≫ ph)
 :
    ∃ s : SpTowerGamma.orderedLine l E b X wh (d + e) ≅
      (SpTowerShriek.tensor l E b X).obj
        ((SpTowerShriek.pull l E b (o.geometry (jf ≫ pf))).obj
          (SpTowerGamma.orderedLine l E b Y wg e),
          SpTowerGamma.orderedLine l E b X wf d),
      TowerSplitNormalized l E b o q jf pf jg pg jh ph d e wf wg wh Pf Pg Ph af ag ah s
